body.statement:
Let \(E\) be the exact multinomial sampling face, meaning that \(q_\star\in\operatorname{relint}(E)\), and suppose \(\pi_z>0\) for both instrument arms.  At every \(q_\star\in\overline{\mathcal Q}\cap E\) satisfying the equivalent conditions of the continuity frontier, the projected full-loss germ handle recovers, with probability tending to one, all and only the incident zero-intercept homogeneous pieces on the relative tangent space \(T\), including pieces at continuous multi-path switches and propensity--grid ties.  It thereby defines a finite positively homogeneous piecewise-linear map \(\psi_{q_\star}:T\to\mathbb R_+\) such that
\[
\sqrt n\,d_H(S(\widetilde q),S(q_\star))\ \Rightarrow\ \psi_{q_\star}(G).
\]
If the relative multinomial covariance is estimated by its plug-in value on the same exact face, conditional Gaussian simulation of the recovered germ and a closed upper \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile, with a vanishing nonnegative numerical guard, gives a pointwise asymptotically valid Hausdorff ball.  The exact-face condition includes lower-dimensional structural-zero faces; if a larger face than the true sampling face is used, this conclusion need not hold.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(Q_E=\overline{\mathcal Q}\cap E\) and
\[
f(u,q)=d_H(S(P_Eu),S(q)),\qquad (u,q)\in\operatorname{aff}(E)\times Q_E.
\]
We first prove that the handle has a finite exact object to recover.  By the path theorem, membership in either set inside the Hausdorff distance is a finite disjunction of systems of affine equalities and inequalities.  The relation \(f(u,q)\le r\) is expressed by the two quantified directed-excess formulas
\[
\forall a\in S(P_Eu)\ \exists b\in S(q):\|a-b\|_\infty\le r,
\quad
\forall b\in S(q)\ \exists a\in S(P_Eu):\|a-b\|_\infty\le r.
\tag{1}
\]
Euclidean projection onto the fixed polyhedron \(Q_E\) is characterized by finitely many active-set affine systems and their normal-cone inequalities.  Substituting those systems into (1) and eliminating its finitely many linear quantifiers produces a finite semilinear graph.  A single-valued semilinear graph admits a finite relatively polyhedral partition on whose cells
\[
f(u,q)=a_j^{\mathsf T}u+b_j^{\mathsf T}q+c_j.
\tag{2}
\]
This follows constructively by distributing the resulting Boolean formula into polyhedral cells and solving each graph equality for its single value.  Thus the primal--dual compilation in the handle loses no path, projection face, or distance piece.

Let the boundary of cell \(j\) be described by affine forms \(\ell_{jr}(u,q)\).  On the diagonal define
\[
\delta_{jr}(q)=\ell_{jr}(q,q),\qquad
\eta_j(q)=(a_j+b_j)^{\mathsf T}q+c_j.
\tag{3}
\]
These are exactly the normalized diagonal boundary and value-intercept forms included by the handle.  The continuity frontier supplies \(H,\varepsilon>0\) with
\[
d_H(S(q'),S(q_\star))\le H\|q'-q_\star\|
\quad(q'\in Q_E,\ \|q'-q_\star\|<\varepsilon).
\tag{4}
\]
Projection is nonexpansive and fixes \(q_\star\), so (4) implies
\[
0\le f(q_\star+v,q_\star)\le H\|v\|
\tag{5}
\]
for all sufficiently small feasible \(v\in T\).  If the closure of a cell in (2) is incident to \((q_\star,q_\star)\) through such first-coordinate perturbations, (5) and continuity of its affine extension force \(\eta_j(q_\star)=0\).  A cell with a nonzero diagonal boundary gap is not incident locally.  For every zero boundary form and zero value intercept, substitution of \((u,q)=(q_\star+v,q_\star)\) in (2)--(3) gives respectively
\[
\ell_{jr}(q_\star+v,q_\star)=a_{jr}^{\mathsf T}v,\qquad
f(q_\star+v,q_\star)=a_j^{\mathsf T}v.
\tag{6}
\]
Consequently the incident cells cut \(T\) into finitely many cones, and (6) defines a finite positively homogeneous piecewise-linear function \(\psi_{q_\star}\).  Finiteness of the nonzero gaps gives one radius on which
\[
f(q_\star+v,q_\star)=\psi_{q_\star}(v).
\tag{7}
\]
Conversely, every retained cone comes from an incident cell of the exact graph, so (7) retains all and only the reachable zero-intercept pieces.

This description is constant on a diagonal stratum.  Indeed, if \(q\) stays in the stratum determined by the signs, including zeros, of all forms in (3), every nonzero form retains its sign, every zero form remains identically zero on the stratum, and after translation by \(v\) its boundary and value reduce to the same fixed linear forms as in (6).  Hence the incident cones and their slopes are unchanged.  This proves the asserted common homogeneous germ at multi-path switches, at grid ties, and on relative lower-dimensional cells.

We next verify snapping.  Because \(q_\star\in\operatorname{relint}(E)\), every nonstructural multinomial cell is positive.  For a bounded cell-indicator vector \(W_i\), expansion of its characteristic function gives
\[
\mathbb E\exp\{i t^{\mathsf T}(W_i-\mathbb EW_i)/\sqrt n\}
=1-\frac{t^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Var}(W_i)t}{2n}+o(n^{-1}).
\]
Taking the \(n\)-th power and applying the ratio expansion from joint cell shares to arm-conditional shares yields
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat q-q_\star)\Rightarrow G,\qquad
\Sigma_z=\{\operatorname{diag}(q_{\star z})-q_{\star z}q_{\star z}^{\mathsf T}\}/\pi_z
\tag{8}
\]
on the relative normalization tangent space.  The denominators are nonzero with probability tending to one because \(\pi_z>0\).  Projection nonexpansiveness gives \(\widetilde q-q_\star=O_p(n^{-1/2})\).  For each of the finitely many affine diagonal forms, therefore,
\[
\delta(\widetilde q)=O_p(n^{-1/2})\quad\text{if }\delta(q_\star)=0,
\]
whereas \(|\delta(\widetilde q)|\) is eventually separated from zero if \(\delta(q_\star)\ne0\); the same holds for \(\eta\).  Since \(\sqrt n\kappa_n\to\infty\) and \(\kappa_n\to0\), snapping selects exactly the true zero forms and the correct nonzero signs with probability tending to one.  The recovered function consequently equals \(\psi_{q_\star}\) with probability tending to one.

On the event \(\widehat q\) lies in the local region, positive homogeneity and (7) give the exact equality
\[
\sqrt n\,d_H(S(\widetilde q),S(q_\star))
=\psi_{q_\star}\!\left(\sqrt n(\widehat q-q_\star)\right).
\tag{9}
\]
The discontinuity set of a finite piecewise-linear function is contained in finitely many proper linear subspaces.  Exact-face positivity makes \(\Sigma\) positive definite on \(T\), so those subspaces have \(G\)-probability zero.  Equations (8)--(9) prove the asserted weak limit.

The plug-in multinomial covariance is consistent on the same face.  Conditional Gaussian laws with that covariance converge to the law of \(G\), and the recovered germ is eventually the true one.  A homogeneous linear piece can create no positive atom under a nondegenerate Gaussian; zero pieces can create only an atom at zero.  Hence the law of \(\psi_{q_\star}(G)\) is continuous on \((0,\infty)\).  At a positive upper quantile, ordinary quantile convergence applies.  If the upper quantile is zero, its definition implies \(\Pr\{\psi_{q_\star}(G)=0\}\ge1-\alpha\); using a closed ball and a vanishing nonnegative guard preserves the inequality.  Thus the simulated ball has pointwise limiting coverage at least \(1-\alpha\).

If \(E\) is larger than the true sampling face, \(\Sigma\) is singular in undeclared zero directions and those directions can lie on loss boundaries with positive limiting probability.  Simulating a nondegenerate law on the larger tangent space then need not reproduce (9).  This proves both the positive exact-face result and the stated limitation.
